archivedDraft.scene: Sam orders with two companions at a café and checks the server’s readback.

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: ミルク入りのコーヒー

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Common in Mexico and the US; pastry is also pan dulce.
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: pan dulce (a sweet roll or pastry)

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: A torta is a sandwich on a roll.
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: ham torta (a sandwich on a roll)

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Quiero pedir para todos, por favor.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: I want to order for everyone, please.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 全員分の注文をお願いします。
注文は合っていますか。
これは彼女の分ですよね。

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Use sin to remove an ingredient.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: チーズ抜きでお願いします。

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Can you repeat the order, please?
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Puede is the polite usted form.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 注文を復唱していただけますか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Could you repeat the order, please?

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: お会計をお願いします。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Estoy en un café con mi esposa, mi hijo y mi suegra.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: I am in a café with my wife, my son, and my mother-in-law.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私は妻と息子と義母と一緒にカフェにいます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I am at a café with my wife, son, and mother-in-law.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Primero, le digo al mesero: Quiero pedir para todos, por favor.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: First, I say to the waiter: I want to order for everyone, please.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: まず、ウェイターに「全員分の注文をお願いします」と言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: First I say to the waiter: An order for everyone, please.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Para mí, un café con leche y unos huevos revueltos.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: For me, a coffee with milk and some scrambled eggs.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私はミルク入りのコーヒーとスクランブルエッグをお願いします。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: For me, coffee with milk and scrambled eggs, please.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Para mi esposa, un té y una torta de jamón, sin queso.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: For my wife, a tea and a ham sandwich, without cheese.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 妻にはお茶とチーズ抜きのハムのトルタをお願いします。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: For my wife, tea and a ham torta without cheese, please.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Mi hijo va a tomar jugo de naranja y un pan dulce.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: My son is going to have orange juice and a sweet roll.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 息子はオレンジジュースとパンドゥルセにします。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: My son will have orange juice and pan dulce.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Mi suegra quiere un café descafeinado y pan tostado con mantequilla.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: My mother-in-law wants a decaf coffee and toast with butter.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 義母はデカフェのコーヒーとバター付きのトーストを希望しています。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: My mother-in-law wants decaf coffee and toast with butter.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Después, repito el pedido: ¿Es correcto? El té es para ella, ¿verdad?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Then, I repeat the order: Is that correct? The tea is for her, right?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: それから注文を繰り返します。「合っていますか。お茶は彼女の分ですよね」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Then I repeat the order: Is it correct? The tea is for her, right?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: El mesero sonríe y dice: Todo está bien, enseguida lo traigo.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The waiter smiles and says: Everything is right, I'll bring it right away.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ウェイターはほほえんで「全部合っています。すぐにお持ちします」と言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The waiter smiles and says: Everything is right. I will bring it right away.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Al final, pido la cuenta en la mesa.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: At the end, I ask for the check at the table.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 最後に、テーブルでお会計を頼みます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Finally, I request the check at the table.

japaneseSpecificFocusCandidate: Place and confirm an order for four family members with distinct food and drink requests while preserving each person's assignment.
speakingGoalInternal: Order breakfast for a family or group with different preferences.
sourceConflictInternal: The archived Japanese draft replaces the four-person family scene with Sam and two companions, omits the mother-in-law, substitutes food, and loses the decaf, no-cheese, and check-at-table details. This candidate follows the pinned Spanish/English source instead. The source Reader has the narrator repeat the order; source card 17 separately asks a server to repeat it. Both speech acts are retained rather than treated as interchangeable. The source does not specify the tea type or a city. Pan dulce and torta de jamón remain named foods rather than generic Japanese substitutes. Japanese cafés may use counter payment, but the pinned scene asks for the check at the table.

savedPositionPolicy: Archived draft rows were not registered and have no explicit stable row IDs. New revision-scoped IDs do not authorize saved-item or audio placement migration. This revision's order is frozen; any insertion or reordering requires a new revision.
reviewQuestionsInternal: Confirm polite ウェイター versus neutral 店員 for the source mesero and target speaking register.
Confirm that the service request 全員分の注文をお願いします adequately teaches source Quiero pedir para todos; its literal Japanese gloss does not include want.
Confirm that ミルク入りのコーヒー preserves café con leche without a stronger coffee-style claim.
Review パンドゥルセ and ハムのトルタ pronunciation and explanatory glosses; neither is a generic Japanese pastry or sliced-bread sandwich.
Confirm お茶 as an unspecified tea; do not silently make the source tea black or green.
Confirm デカフェ and the explicit チーズ抜き order, including a distinct food-allergy interpretation only if the source supplies one.
Check the narrator's order repetition against the separate card asking the server to repeat it.
Confirm table-side check request and all four family assignments before any audio or learner release.
